 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP N. BHATT  Date : 14/08/2024  COMMON ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

Since the prayers and issues involved in the present NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined petitions are identical in nature, which are arising out of the same accident, hence, at the request of learned advocates for the parties, the matters are taken up for final consideration and First Appeal No.1222 of 2015 is considered as lead matter.

Therefore,
all the matters are heard together.

2. The present appeal is filed by the appellant - Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 28.11.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Ad-hoc) (Aux.-8), Gandhidham, Kutch in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.503, 504 and 526 of 1999, by which, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions.

3. Brief facts of the case as per claimants are as under:
3.1
This group of First Appeals is arising out of a vehicular accident occurred on 03.05.2019 for near Adipur at about 22:15 hours.

It is the case of the claimant/s that they were going on a scooter and at that time other friends came from opposite side and they were NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED:
14/08/2024 undefined talking in the side of the road.
At that time, one ST bus number GJ-1-Z-2225 driven by the ST driver lost control over the vehicle and dashed with the person standing on the side of the road.
That has resulted into death of 3 persons and one person was injured.
In case of F.A. Nos.1224 of 2015, 1222 of 2015 and 1223 of 2015 the Tribunal at Gandhidham allowed the claim and awarded the amount of compensation.
While in case of F.A. No.69 of 2014 it was conducted by the Tribunal at Bhuj.
The Tribunal at Bhuj has dismissed the claim petition on the premise that the claimant/s has not disclosed the correct facts.
Therefore the legal heirs of the deceased and original claimants have filed FA No.69 of 2014.

4. Learned advocate for the appellant has submitted that FIR is filed by driver of S.T bus, wherein it is clearly mentioned that there were 4 person travailing on the same scooter in rash and negligent manner and dashed with S.T bus.
Therefore, accident occurred.
FIR is registered against the scooter driver.

It is submitted that the Tribunal has not appreciated M.A.C.P 542/95 arising from the common Accident,
which has been rejected on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined 10.09.2013 by MACT Bhuj.
It is also submitted that there is no negligence on the part of S.T Driver.

Police has not flied any complaint against S.T., and Panchnama and Inquest panchnama are not connected with said Gujarat State Road Transport ... vs Chandubhai Lakhubhai Meriya on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114162584/
2 accident.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the Tribunal has not appreciated the deposition of eye witness.
It is also submitted that there is no connection between FIR and Witness.
It is submitted that amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
It is also submitted that in F.A. No.1224 of 2015, it is wrongfully mentioned about injury on left hand and he was doing embroidery work with left hand.
No proof of embroidery work is produced.
In view of the above, he has prayed to allow the present appeals by considering the above- mentioned submissions.
5.1 Learned advocates for the respondents have submitted that the appellant - ST Corporation has restricted the extent of 50% of the awarded amount.
However, in the grounds no reasons are assigned for excessive or higher award except stating that the Tribunal has added in awarding compensation of Rs.4,72,000/-.
Thus the appellant has accepted its NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined liability.
It is also submitted that in fact, four persons were coming on one scooter from the opposite side and had lost control over the vehicle and dashed with the ST bus.
Therefore it is a case of total negligence on the part of the scooter driver.
Therefore the claim petitions be dismissed.
The first contention of the ST Corporation is that the FIR was filed by the driver of the ST Corporation and there he has stated that the scooter had come and dashed with his bus.

Before dealing with this aspect, it would be considered that so far the case of F.A. Nos.1222 to 1224 of 2015 are concerned, even taking the case of the ST Corporation at its best then, those claimants are third-party so far S.T. Corporation is concerned.
It would be a case of joint and several liability and the claimants can claim against any of the tort-feasor.
The question of contributory liability would be a different issue and will not affect the rights of the claimants are concerned.
5.2 It is submitted that it is required to be noted that the incident had taken place at 22:15 hours.
Out of the 4 persons, 3 had died immediately and one was seriously injured and was in the hospital.

Therefore, the complaint NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED:
14/08/2024 undefined was filed by the driver of the ST bus.
Therefore, definitely he would try to protect his skin.
While the only survived injured Chandubhai the respondent No. 1 in FA 1224 of 2015 had reported to the police immediately on discharge and had narrated the incident as contended by the claimants.
The FIR by the ST driver was registered on 04.05.1994 while the injured had given a detailed complaint to the DSP on 08.05.1994.
This is also on record at Exhibit 32.
It is also submitted that the ST driver is an employee of the appellant - GSRTC.
He has not stepped into the witness box.
The GSRTC has also not taken trouble to see that its employee step into the witness box and prove the case of FIR as stated by the said driver.
In absence of such evidence and more particularly its being held back adverse inference will definitely be drawn against the ST driver and the GSRTC.
It is further submitted that the injured and claimant in MACP No. 526 of 1999 has given his evidence on oath that Exhibit 42.
This evidence has been properly appreciated and considered by the Tribunal.
The ST Corporation was not able to dislodge his evidence on oath.

Therefore, the conclusion of the Tribunal to hold the ST Corporation liable for payment NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined of compensation does not require any interference.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal has also appreciated and Gujarat State Road Transport ... vs Chandubhai Lakhubhai Meriya on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114162584/
3 properly considered the facts recorded in the pension at Exhibit 34.

sentences.text: The fact that the scooter was lying on the left side of the bus and was near the edge of the road would make it clear that the negligence was on the part of the ST bus and not of the scooter driver.

Therefore it becomes clear that the ST bus was at excessive speed and could not see the persons standing near the road and at the last moment having seen it he was unable to control the bus to save those people.
Therefore the conclusion that there was sheer negligence on the part of the ST driver is just and proper.
There is no perversity or illegality or any apparent mistake on the face of the record that would call for interference by this Hon'ble Court.
5.3 Additionally, it is submitted that three petitions were filed at Gandhidham while one at Bhuj.
The claimants might not be aware about the petitions being before different tribunals.
However the ST Corporation was aware that petitions are filed before different tribunals in the same district.
The driver of the ST NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined Corporation was also aware that different petitions are filed at different places.
No attempt was made to have the petitions being transferred to one Tribunal.
12. Apart from that the Ld. Tribunal dismissed the MACP 542 of 1995 by judgement and award dated 10/09/2013.
While the Ld. Tribunal at Gandhidham allowed the claim petitions after more than a year on 28/11/2014.
No doubt the decisions may not be binding but the ST Corporation had knowledge and copy of the petition dismissed by Tribunal at Bhuj.
Therefore it should and ought to have drawn the attention of the Tribunal at Gandhidham about the order of the Tribunal at Bhuj.
That has not been done.
Be it as it may.
The appellant ST Corporation has raised a ground that the Ld. tribunal has not considered the judgement and award passed in MACP No. 542 of 1995.
However the said judgement and award or any other oral or documentary evidence has not been produced by the ST Corporation in the group of 3 claim petitions.
Therefore the said submission and contention cannot be considered for any purpose.
Therefore, it is submitted that the presnet appeals filed by the ST Corporation deserves to be dismissed.
The one by the claimant would be required to be remanded back NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined as the Tribunal has not given findings on the issue of quantum.
6. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.
7.1 I have considered the rival submissions made at the bar by the respective parties and gone through the materials available on record.

It transpires that the Tribunal has concluded that the appellant, S.T. Corporation, failed to examine its driver, who could have been the best person to be considered an eyewitness of the actual accident.
I find that the Tribunal has not committed any error in reaching to its conclusion.

Furthermore, the other contentions raised by the appellant Corporation--that the Panchnama and inquest Panchnama are not connected with the said accident--are also not found reliable and are not supported by the material available on record.
The Tribunal has rightly concluded the occurrence of the accident by considering the relevant material.

7.2 Furthermore, one of the contentions of the appellant - corporation is that there is no proof of income produced by the claimant(s), and hence, the compensation NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined regarding the quantum is not just and proper.

Considering the amount awarded by the Gujarat State Road Transport ... vs Chandubhai Lakhubhai Meriya on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114162584/
4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal, I find that the amounts awarded by the Tribunal are on the conservative side given the injuries sustained and the fact that the Tribunal has discussed every aspect in detail.
In the injury case, the Tribunal has considered the surgery performed on the claimant, as well as his age, which were appropriately considered by the Tribunal.
7.3 Moreover, the Tribunal has considered various aspects of the matter in detail.
In cases of fatal accidents, the Tribunal awarded Rs.4,72,000/- and Rs.4,21,000/- only, and in the case of an injury accident, the Tribunal awarded Rs.2,13,500/- only.
These amounts should have been on the higher side.

Therefore, considering the facts of the case and the fact that a higher amount could have been awarded, and given the fact that no cross-objection has been filed in the present proceedings, I am not granting any further compensation, although,
under the principle of just compensation, the claimants are entitled to a higher amount.

Hence,
regarding the aspect of quantum, the present appeals are found to be merit-less.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined 7.4

Regarding other aspects where S.T. Corporation has challenged the judgment and award passed by other Tribunals in other claim petitions, where the Tribunal had dismissed the claimant's petition on the grounds of suppression of material facts, it must be noted that such a contention is to be negated.
This is particularly relevant considering the observations made in another claim petition in First Appeal No.69 of 2014, which should be considered as part of the reasoning in this appeal as well.
Moreover, considering the reasons given by the Tribunal, I find that there is not error in the reasoning given by the Tribunal, and no interference is required to be called for.
Therefore, as the present appeals are found merits less and therefore, the present appeals are required to be dismissed.
8. In view of the above, the present captioned First Appeals are dismissed with no order as to costs.

9. The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, pursuant to the order of this Court if any,
shall be disbursed to the claimant/s, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1224/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 14/08/2024 undefined within a period of six weeks from today.
10. Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) DIWAKAR SHUKLA Gujarat State Road Transport ... vs Chandubhai Lakhubhai Meriya on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114162584/
